subject: Discrepancy: March marketplace metering vs invoice offsets
messages:
From: Acme Analytics <acme-billing@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: March AWS Marketplace - metering numbers don’t match offsets

Hi Jordan,

We pulled the March payout and noticed the ‘offset’ line on the AWS invoice is larger than the metered usage we see in our internal ledger. Specifically, the AWS invoice shows $24,180 in marketplace offsets for the March 2029 invoice, while our metering report (attached) sums to $21,300. That leaves a $2,880 gap that AWS applied as an offset on our payout.

Can you help confirm whether Redwood passed any marketplace credits or merchant-level adjustments that would explain the delta? We need this to reconcile with our finance team and to understand if this will impact our April remittance.

Attached: acme_march_metering.csv (metering export from Acme) and acme_invoice_202903.pdf

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Billing Operations — Acme Analytics
acme-billing@acmeanalytics.com
[Attachment: acme_march_metering.csv]
[Attachment: acme_invoice_202903.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <acme-billing@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: March AWS Marketplace - metering numbers don’t match offsets

Thanks Priya — appreciate the quick heads up and the attachments. Looping in finance and marketplace ops to triage (Laura, Ben, Marissa).

Initial ask: can you confirm the Acme entity ID used in the marketplace listing and whether you had any promo/credit lines applied in March? That will help us trace offsets back to any partner credits or marketplace fee adjustments.

Ben/Marissa/Laura — can you start by comparing Acme’s March merchant adjustments vs. what AWS reported as offsets? I’ll request the AWS invoice detail if needed. If we find a Redwood-initiated credit (e.g., passthrough credit or pilot credit) we should record it against DEAL-2029-0147 and loop revenue ops.

Next step: I’ll ask AWS for the metering->offset line level detail and share the response.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: March AWS Marketplace - metering numbers don’t match offsets

Forwarding notes from initial ledger pass. Summary: our merchant ledger shows two manual adjustments posted on 2029-03-29 for Acme: a $1,200 promotional credit applied to a pilot listing, and a $900 correction for an earlier overcharge (internal reversal). That totals $2,100 of offsets from Redwood’s side. AWS additionally applied a platform fee reserve reversal of $780 on 2029-04-05 that they list as an offset on the March statement. Together that explains $2,880 gap (1,200 + 900 + 780).

I attached my reconciliation workbook that maps the ledger entries to invoice rows. See tab ‘mapping’ for row-level matches to Acme's CSV. Two small caveats:
- The $900 reversal originated from a refund we issued to Acme that was applied against the ledger but the refund entry is coded differently in the AWS feed (refund vs. credit).
- Promo credit was applied to a pilot SKUs; the AWS report aggregates by merchant and hides SKU detail in the summary.

Attaching: 20290506-jb-ledger-recon.xlsx

Ben
[Attachment: 20290506-jb-ledger-recon.xlsx]

From: Acme Analytics <acme-billing@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Partner Support <aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 6 May 2029 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: March AWS Marketplace - metering numbers don’t match offsets

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick triage and for Ben’s workbook. I reviewed the mapping vs. our metering export and that reconciles cleanly on our side. Two follow-ups:

1) For audit purposes, can Redwood provide the GL/account codes you used for the $1,200 promo credit and the $900 refund adjustment? Our tax group needs the coding to validate VAT treatment for Q1.

2) The $780 AWS platform fee reversal — can you confirm whether that is an AWS-initiated adjustment (we also see a note from AWS support) or whether Redwood requested that reversal? If AWS initiated it, we’ll take it up with AWS but wanted to confirm.

If you can send the GL codes and a one-page reconciliation summary we’ll close the case on our side and proceed with April remittance.

Thanks,
Priya
[Attachment: none]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <acme-billing@acmeanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: March AWS Marketplace - metering numbers don’t match offsets

Priya — thanks for confirming. Ben and Marissa confirmed the GL mappings and I’ve pasted the one-page summary below for your records. We did not request the $780 AWS platform reversal; that came from AWS and is out-of-band from Redwood. We will include the reversal detail with the supporting AWS case ID when we share the packet.

One-page reconciliation (summary):
- AWS invoice offset (March 2029): $24,180
- Acme metering export (per Acme): $21,300
- Redwood-origin adjustments:
  - Pilot promo credit (GL 6402-PROMO): $1,200
  - Refund reversal (GL 5120-REV): $900
- AWS platform fee reversal (AWS case #12345678): $780
- Total reconciled: $21,300 + $1,200 + $900 + $780 = $24,180

Action items: 
- Jordan (me): compile support packet (Ben/Marissa to add ledger extracts + GL entries) and send to Acme and AWS (expected EOD Wed).
- Acme: confirm receipt and file for VAT team if needed (Priya).
- Marissa: add the AWS case ID and raw feed extract to the packet.

We’ll mark DEAL-2029-0147 as reconciled for March once the packet is shared. If anything else shows up during April’s remittance we’ll reopen.

Thanks all — good teamwork.

Jordan 
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Ben/Marissa ledger extracts to follow]
